subject.title: fix(mcp): stop ignored disabled servers from starting

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make legacy MCP `disabled` configurations fail validation unless the guarded doctor/update migration can rewrite their owning file?
rationale: The implementation is correct under repository policy, but this is an observable upgrade contract: unsupported include layouts stop at validation and require operator action rather than retaining silent startup behavior.

options.title: Accept guarded fail-closed migration
options.body: Land after rebasing and green exact-head checks, accepting validation failure for ambiguous include ownership as safer than silent process startup or config flattening.

options.title: Require broader automatic migration
options.body: Hold the PR and define additional safe ownership rules for complex include layouts before making `disabled` fail validation.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded fail-closed migration
recommendation.body: Land after rebasing and green exact-head checks, accepting validation failure for ambiguous include ownership as safer than silent process startup or config flattening.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the prior MCP operator-control work that established the canonical configuration contract affected by this upgrade choice.
